p: Read Ps 32:1.
law: The prophet under the name of a teacher calls the people his, and the doctrine his, as Paul calls the gospel his, of which he was but the preacher, as in Rom 2:16,16:25.
fathers have told us: Who were the people of God.
testimony in Jacob: By the testimony and law, he means your law written, which they were commanded to teach their children, De 6:7.
generation to come might know them: He shows how the children would be like their father's: that is, in maintaining God's pure religion.
set their hope in God: He shows where the use of this doctrine exists: in faith, in the meditation of God's benefits, and in obedience.

fathers: Though these fathers were the seed of Abraham and the chosen people, yet he shows by their rebellion, provocation, falsehood, and hypocrisy, that the children should not follow their examples.

Ephraim: By Ephraim he means also the rest of the tribes, because they were most in number: whose punishment declares that they were unfaithful to God, and by their multitude and authority had corrupted all others.
fathers: He proves that not only the posterity but also their forefathers were wicked and rebellious to God.
sinned yet more against him by: Their wicked malice could be overcome by no benefits, which were great and many.
asking meat for their lust: Then to require more than is necessary, and to separate God's power from his will, is to tempt God.
furnish a table in the wilderness: Thus when we give place to sin, we are moved to doubt God's power, unless he is always ready to serve our lust.
trusted not in his salvation: That is, in his fatherly providence, by which he cares for his, and provides sufficiently.
clouds from above: So that they had that which was necessary and sufficient: but their lust made them cover that which they knew God had denied them.
east wind to blow in the: God used the wind to show them that all the elements were at his command, and that no distance could restrain his working.
lust: Such is the nature of concupiscence, that the more it has the more it lusts.
the fattest of them: Though others were not spared, yet chiefly they suffered, who trusted in their strength against God.
sinned still: Thus sin by continuance makes man insensible, so that by no plagues they can be amended.
slew them: Such was their hypocrisy, that they sought God out of fear of punishment, though in their heart they did not love him.
heart was not right with him: Whatever does not come from the pure fountain of the heart is hypocrisy.
forgave their iniquity: Because he would always have some remnant of a Church to praise his Name in earth, he did not permit their sins to overcome his mercy.
turned back and tempted God: That is, they often tempted him.
limited the Holy One of Israel: As they all do who measure the power of God by their capacity.
remembered not his hand: The forgetfulness of God's benefits is the root of rebellion and all vice.
divers sorts of flies among them: This word signifies a confused mixture of flies and venomous worms. Some take it for all sorts of serpents: some for all wild beasts.
gave also their increase unto the: He does not repeat here all the miracles that God did in Egypt, but certain which might be sufficient to convince the people of malice and ingratitude.
evil angels among them: So called either for the effect, that is, of punishing the wicked: or else because they were wicked spirits, whom God permitted to vex men.
chief of their strength in the: The firstborn are so called, as in Ge 49:3.
Ham: That is, Egypt: for it was called Mizraim, or Egypt of Mizraim that was the son of Ham.
feared not: That is, they had no opportunity to fear, even as God destroyed their enemies and delivered them falsely.
sanctuary: Meaning, Canaan, which God had consecrated to himself and appointed to his people.
unfaithfully like their fathers: Nothing more displeases God in the children, than when they continue in that wickedness, which their fathers had begun.
provoked him to anger with their: By serving God other than he had appointed.
forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh: For their ingratitude he permitted the Philistines to take the Ark which was the sign of his presence, from among them.
strength into captivity: The Ark is called his power and beauty because by this he defended his people, and beautifully appeared to them.
consumed their young men: They were suddenly destroyed, 1Sa 4:10.
given to marriage: They had no marriage songs: that is, they were not married.
widows made no lamentation: Either they were slain before or taken prisoner by their enemies, and so were forbidden.

shouteth by reason of wine: Because they were drunk in their sins, they judged God's patience to be slumbering, as though he were drunk, therefore he answering their beastly judgment, says, he will awake and take sudden vengeance.
Joseph: Showing that he did not spare the Israelites altogether, though he punished their enemies.
built his sanctuary like high palaces: By building the temple, and establishing the kingdom, he declares that the signs of his favour were among them.
he fed them according to the: He shows where a kings charge stands: that is, to provide faithfully for his people, to guide them by counsel, and defend them by power.
